world.title: U.S. launches Iron Gate task force to curb Iran’s land supply routes
world.summary: The U.S. military has formed Task Force Iron Gate, a team of about 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida, to coordinate efforts to restrict Iran’s movement of weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned goods and illicit revenue over land and across the Caspian Sea. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said
world.content: The U.S. military has formed Task Force Iron Gate, a team of about 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida, to coordinate efforts to restrict Iran’s movement of weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned goods and illicit revenue over land and across the Caspian Sea. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said the team would work with other government agencies, expanding Washington’s pressure campaign beyond its months-long naval blockade. The command says the blockade has prevented more than $25 billion in Iranian crude oil exports. A Reuters investigation cited by The Globe and Mail found that Iran had imported at least $2 billion in military-related equipment since January 2025 through routes that bypassed the blockade and Western sanctions. The military has not explained how Iron Gate will disrupt overland trade or whether it will involve ground operations. The move follows an August U.S. Treasury pressure campaign targeting digital assets, gold, technology, aviation and shipping. Qatar continues to mediate between Washington and Tehran. Its prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, said the sides should pursue an achievable agreement. Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said he had spoken with counterparts from 12 countries in the preceding 48 hours.
world.image_alt: U.S. launches Iron Gate task force to curb Iran’s land supply routes

world.title: Gaza storm floods 70,000 displacement tents, leaving families without shelter
world.summary: Heavy rain and strong winds flooded about 70,000 tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in Gaza on Saturday, Nov. 7, leaving tens of thousands without dry shelter, according to Gaza’s Hamas-run government media office. Civil defence said it received more than 1,500 calls for help overnight. Damaged walls and roofs col
world.content: Heavy rain and strong winds flooded about 70,000 tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in Gaza on Saturday, Nov. 7, leaving tens of thousands without dry shelter, according to Gaza’s Hamas-run government media office. Civil defence said it received more than 1,500 calls for help overnight. Damaged walls and roofs collapsed, injuring people, and families fled inundated camps. Fuel shortages, damaged equipment and a lack of pumps are hampering the response, according to Gaza municipal and civil-defence officials. Humanitarian workers and residents warned that soaked bedding, cold and rainwater mixed with sewage pose heightened risks to children and other vulnerable people. Gaza officials say Israel has restricted the entry of prefabricated homes and heavy equipment. Israel’s aid-coordination agency said it had coordinated additional sewage-pumping vehicles and sanitation work before the storm. A ceasefire took effect on Oct. 10, 2025, but negotiations over Hamas disarmament and an Israeli troop withdrawal remain unresolved. Gaza emergency committee member Mustafa Qazzaat said the territory urgently needs 200,000 prefabricated homes, along with machinery, electricity and heating.
world.image_alt: Gaza storm floods 70,000 displacement tents, leaving families without shelter

world.title: Democratic midterm wins put Trump’s Iran war under scrutiny
world.summary: Democrats won control of both chambers of the U.S. Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, giving them investigative and spending powers when the new Congress convenes in January. Analysts say Congress has limited power to direct President Donald Trump’s foreign policy, including on Iran, Ukraine and trade. The Iran
world.content: Democrats won control of both chambers of the U.S. Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, giving them investigative and spending powers when the new Congress convenes in January. Analysts say Congress has limited power to direct President Donald Trump’s foreign policy, including on Iran, Ukraine and trade. The Iran war contributed to Republican losses as voters faced higher energy costs. Vice President JD Vance blamed the war for the defeat, while Trump acknowledged gas prices played a role but said he would make the same decision again. Trump has threatened renewed attacks on Iran, and officials and analysts disagree on whether the election will constrain him or make him more willing to escalate. Trilateral talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine are planned for Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday.
world.image_alt: Democratic midterm wins put Trump’s Iran war under scrutiny

world.title: France probes possible foreign links to Europe-wide airline bomb hoaxes
world.summary: French prosecutors opened an investigation on Saturday into hoax bomb threats against commercial flights across Europe, seeking to identify the email senders and determine whether they had links to foreign powers. Dozens of flights were diverted, searched or escorted by military aircraft during the week; authorities re
world.content: French prosecutors opened an investigation on Saturday into hoax bomb threats against commercial flights across Europe, seeking to identify the email senders and determine whether they had links to foreign powers. Dozens of flights were diverted, searched or escorted by military aircraft during the week; authorities reported no explosives and no injuries. Threats also reached European broadcasters on Friday, prompting evacuations at Ireland’s RTÉ and Bulgaria’s Nova TV. Some airline-threat emails used the name “fighters of the Male State,” a reference to a Russian far-right group, but the group’s founder, Vladislav Pozdniakov, denied involvement. Authorities have not publicly attributed the flight threats to a state or organization. Separately, cyberattacks disrupted supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries. Ireland’s government described the threats as likely part of a coordinated disruption campaign, while European Union officials said it was too early to conclude whether the incidents were linked. Security experts were due to meet in Brussels next week to discuss responses to the hoaxes as the French investigation continues.
world.image_alt: France probes possible foreign links to Europe-wide airline bomb hoaxes

world.title: Central Japan quake injures 22, prompts warning of stronger aftershocks
world.summary: A magnitude-5.7 earthquake struck western Shizuoka Prefecture in central Japan at 1:04 a.m. Sunday, injuring at least 22 people in Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures, local authorities said. The Japan Meteorological Agency put the quake’s magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey reported 5.5. The quake struck at
world.content: A magnitude-5.7 earthquake struck western Shizuoka Prefecture in central Japan at 1:04 a.m. Sunday, injuring at least 22 people in Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures, local authorities said. The Japan Meteorological Agency put the quake’s magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey reported 5.5. The quake struck at a depth of about 40 kilometers. No tsunami warning was issued. The shaking affected a broad area, including Hamamatsu and parts of Kyoto, Nara, Yamanashi and Gifu. Store windows shattered, books fell from shelves and some people were injured while fleeing down stairs. Aichi recorded the strongest shaking; Tokyo did not feel the quake. The Japan Meteorological Agency warned residents to prepare for possible strong quakes over the coming week, particularly in the next two to three days, and to watch for landslides and falling rocks. Local trains were suspended and bullet trains slowed for safety checks. JR Central said the Tokaido Shinkansen returned to normal speeds before noon.
world.image_alt: Central Japan quake injures 22, prompts warning of stronger aftershocks

world.title: Pope Leo urges South Americans to bridge divides during 12-day tour
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV urged South Americans to bridge political and social divides on Saturday, celebrating Mass before about 40,000 people in Paysandú, Uruguay, on the first full day of his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. He invoked the bridge linking Uruguay and Argentina and the shared custom of drinking mate as
world.content: Pope Leo XIV urged South Americans to bridge political and social divides on Saturday, celebrating Mass before about 40,000 people in Paysandú, Uruguay, on the first full day of his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. He invoked the bridge linking Uruguay and Argentina and the shared custom of drinking mate as symbols of dialogue and community. The visit is the first papal trip to Uruguay since 1988 and seeks to strengthen the Catholic Church’s presence in one of Latin America’s most secular countries. In Montevideo, Leo visited the Casavalle neighborhood, where parish groups provide housing, job opportunities and drug rehabilitation. He said children in Uruguay can fear they will not return home from school and urged the community to support people in need. Leo also called for universal access to health care, drawing on his recent lung-cancer surgery. He is due to travel to Argentina on Sunday, then continue to Peru; the tour is scheduled to end November 17.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo urges South Americans to bridge divides during 12-day tour

world.title: Houthi authorities report 33 killed in Saudi strikes near Sanaa
world.summary: Houthi authorities said airstrikes hit homes in al-Shariya village, east of Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, killing 33 people and wounding 39 on Saturday. The reported toll includes 13 children and eight women. The figures and the claim that Saudi Arabia carried out the strikes could not be independently verified. Saudi Arabia
world.content: Houthi authorities said airstrikes hit homes in al-Shariya village, east of Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, killing 33 people and wounding 39 on Saturday. The reported toll includes 13 children and eight women. The figures and the claim that Saudi Arabia carried out the strikes could not be independently verified. Saudi Arabia’s Center for International Communication said it was investigating the report. The Houthi-run health ministry said strikes also hit rescue workers as they searched the rubble. Abdul-Aziz al-Dailami, director of Sehatuna Hospital in Sanaa, said victims remained trapped. The Houthis and government forces blamed each other for Friday’s attack on a market in Taiz province, where at least 30 people were reported killed. Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces resumed in July, ending a 2022 U.N.-brokered truce. The Houthis said they launched missile and drone attacks in retaliation; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile headed toward Riyadh. The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since the fighting resumed.
world.image_alt: Houthi authorities report 33 killed in Saudi strikes near Sanaa

world.title: New Zealand election leaves governing coalition one seat above majority threshold
world.summary: New Zealand’s Nov. 7 election left Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s National-led coalition with 67 of 131 parliamentary seats in the provisional count, one more than the 66 needed for a majority. The opposition Labour-led bloc remained short of power. About 14% of ballots—nearly 400,000 special votes, including overs
world.content: New Zealand’s Nov. 7 election left Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s National-led coalition with 67 of 131 parliamentary seats in the provisional count, one more than the 66 needed for a majority. The opposition Labour-led bloc remained short of power. About 14% of ballots—nearly 400,000 special votes, including overseas and out-of-electorate ballots—remain to be counted. The Electoral Commission has set Nov. 27 for the official result. National and Labour each received just under 30% of the party vote, while the centrist Opportunity Party, led by political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is projected to enter Parliament with seven seats. If special votes erase the governing bloc’s narrow lead, Opportunity could become pivotal. Wong says she is open to working with either side, and Luxon has softened his previous refusal to engage with her party. Luxon will remain head of a caretaker government until a new administration is formed. Parties have said formal coalition talks must wait for the final count, and negotiations could continue for weeks. The caretaker government is expected to handle routine business in the meantime.
world.image_alt: New Zealand election leaves governing coalition one seat above majority threshold

business.title: IRS raises 2027 tax bracket thresholds while rates remain unchanged
business.summary: The Internal Revenue Service raised federal income-tax bracket thresholds for tax year 2027, allowing taxpayers to earn more before entering a higher bracket; tax rates remain unchanged. The thresholds will rise about 3.2%, compared with a 2% increase for 2026, according to IRS figures reported by MarketWatch. The annu
business.content: The Internal Revenue Service raised federal income-tax bracket thresholds for tax year 2027, allowing taxpayers to earn more before entering a higher bracket; tax rates remain unchanged. The thresholds will rise about 3.2%, compared with a 2% increase for 2026, according to IRS figures reported by MarketWatch. The annual inflation adjustments are intended to prevent wage increases that merely keep pace with prices from pushing taxpayers into higher marginal tax brackets. Tax rates on long-term investment gains remain 0%, 15% and 20%, while the income thresholds for each rate will change in 2027.
business.image_alt: IRS raises 2027 tax bracket thresholds while rates remain unchanged

business.title: Berkshire shares climb as investors shift away from AI stocks
business.summary: Berkshire Hathaway shares have outperformed the S&P 500 as investors moved away from technology stocks amid concerns about AI spending. The conglomerate’s Class B shares rose 13.6% this year, while the benchmark gained 7.8%; since Oct. 1, Berkshire advanced 14% as the S&P fell about 4%. Berkshire reported $9.4 billion
business.content: Berkshire Hathaway shares have outperformed the S&P 500 as investors moved away from technology stocks amid concerns about AI spending. The conglomerate’s Class B shares rose 13.6% this year, while the benchmark gained 7.8%; since Oct. 1, Berkshire advanced 14% as the S&P fell about 4%. Berkshire reported $9.4 billion in third-quarter investment gains, down 46% from a year earlier, and bought back $9.6 billion of its shares—more than twice the previous quarter’s total. Chief Executive Greg Abel continued reducing the company’s cash holdings. A more detailed filing later in November is expected to disclose Berkshire’s individual third-quarter stock trades.
business.image_alt: Berkshire shares climb as investors shift away from AI stocks

business.title: ECB chief warns inflation will remain high as December rate decision nears
business.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said inflation is likely to remain high in coming quarters, warning that a prolonged period of high prices would increase risks to the bank’s medium-term target. Euro-area headline inflation reached 4% in October, according to To Vima, while core inflation held at 2.5%,
business.content: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said inflation is likely to remain high in coming quarters, warning that a prolonged period of high prices would increase risks to the bank’s medium-term target. Euro-area headline inflation reached 4% in October, according to To Vima, while core inflation held at 2.5%, according to Globo. Lagarde said the ECB will examine detailed data before its December interest-rate decision; she did not commit to another increase. Several ECB officials have signaled that a further quarter-point increase is possible, following two such moves since energy costs surged after the war in Iran. But Lagarde said wage agreements and companies’ pay expectations have not indicated inflationary pressures beyond those the bank had projected. She also said energy-price futures and long-term interest rates have risen since the ECB’s September forecasts, potentially affecting both inflation and growth.
business.image_alt: ECB chief warns inflation will remain high as December rate decision nears

business.title: China forecasts $940 billion energy investment as grid spending grows
business.summary: China is projected to invest $940 billion in energy in 2026, more than any other country, according to the Global Energy Transition Report 2026, released by the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society and reported by state broadcaster CCTV. Spending is shifting toward power grids and infrastructure to connect r
business.content: China is projected to invest $940 billion in energy in 2026, more than any other country, according to the Global Energy Transition Report 2026, released by the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society and reported by state broadcaster CCTV. Spending is shifting toward power grids and infrastructure to connect renewable generation; the International Energy Agency expects Chinese grid investment to reach about $140 billion this year. China had 2.337 billion kilowatts of installed renewable capacity at the end of 2025, 60.1% of total power capacity. Renewable sources generated 3.99 trillion kilowatt-hours, or 38.3% of electricity output, and growth in renewable generation covered the increase in electricity consumption. Coal-fired power supplied 49.7% of electricity in the first half of 2026, the first time its share fell below half, while energy-related carbon dioxide emissions fell 0.5% in 2025.
business.image_alt: China forecasts $940 billion energy investment as grid spending grows

business.title: US inflation reports and AI cloud earnings set key market tests
business.summary: U.S. inflation reports and earnings from artificial-intelligence cloud-computing providers are due next week, as investors watch for clues to the Federal Reserve’s next interest-rate decision. The consumer price index is due Tuesday and the producer price index Friday. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect consumer p
business.content: U.S. inflation reports and earnings from artificial-intelligence cloud-computing providers are due next week, as investors watch for clues to the Federal Reserve’s next interest-rate decision. The consumer price index is due Tuesday and the producer price index Friday. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect consumer prices to rise 0.3% in October, slowing from September’s 0.6% increase, the largest monthly gain since April. AI cloud-computing providers CoreWeave and Nebius are also due to report, with investors seeking details on spending, financing and project progress.

business.title: Tesla winds down Cybertruck production as electric pickup demand weakens
business.summary: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around mid-2027, Chief Executive Elon Musk said, freeing space to build more Cybercab robotaxis. The company has not said whether it will move Cybertruck production elsewhere or end the model entirely. U.S. Cybertruck sales fell to 20,237 in 2025, down 48%
business.content: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around mid-2027, Chief Executive Elon Musk said, freeing space to build more Cybercab robotaxis. The company has not said whether it will move Cybertruck production elsewhere or end the model entirely. U.S. Cybertruck sales fell to 20,237 in 2025, down 48% from 2024 and far short of Musk’s once-stated goal of 250,000 a year. Cox Automotive estimated sales of 11,586 in the first nine months of 2026. Six electric pickup models tracked by Cox Automotive sold about 32,500 units through September, 53% fewer than a year earlier, while automakers have cut or canceled other full-size electric trucks. Tesla says it will use the factory space for autonomous vehicles, but the Cybercab is still under review by U.S. safety regulators.
business.image_alt: Tesla winds down Cybertruck production as electric pickup demand weakens

business.title: U.S. job growth raises odds of December Federal Reserve rate hike
business.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than twice economists’ expectations, while unemployment fell to 4.1%. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year earlier, below the 3.7% increase in consumer prices reported by the Korea Herald. Markets priced in an 80% chance of a quarter-point increase at the Fede
business.content: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than twice economists’ expectations, while unemployment fell to 4.1%. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year earlier, below the 3.7% increase in consumer prices reported by the Korea Herald. Markets priced in an 80% chance of a quarter-point increase at the Federal Reserve’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, up from 67% on Thursday. Concerns about a slowdown linked to artificial intelligence (AI) had previously reduced rate-hike bets. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said further tightening was likely, while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has said policymakers would assess incoming data before deciding.
business.image_alt: U.S. job growth raises odds of December Federal Reserve rate hike

business.title: Novartis to halt pelacarsen development for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease after trial finds no benefit
business.summary: Novartis will stop developing pelacarsen to prevent heart attacks and other cardiovascular events after a large trial found the drug did not reduce serious outcomes, despite sharply lowering lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a), a genetically linked blood particle. Results presented Nov. 7 in Chicago showed no meaningful differenc
business.content: Novartis will stop developing pelacarsen to prevent heart attacks and other cardiovascular events after a large trial found the drug did not reduce serious outcomes, despite sharply lowering lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a), a genetically linked blood particle. Results presented Nov. 7 in Chicago showed no meaningful difference in heart attacks, strokes, cardiovascular deaths or urgent artery procedures among 8,350 participants followed for a median of 4.7 years. The company will continue a separate trial in people with aortic valve disease. High Lp(a) affects an estimated one in five people worldwide, and no treatment specifically targets it. A separate Novo Nordisk trial found that its anti-inflammatory drug ziltivekimab did not prevent major heart events, despite reducing inflammation as intended. Other Lp(a) drugs remain in development: Amgen expects Phase 3 results in early 2028, and Eli Lilly expects its results in 2029.
business.image_alt: Novartis to halt pelacarsen development for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease after trial finds no benefit

science.title: Seismic study finds two deep tears in Arabian Plate beneath Iran
science.summary: Researchers have identified two deep tears in the Arabian Plate beneath southeastern Iran, where the Zagros collision zone meets the Makran subduction zone. The structures offer evidence of the transition from oceanic subduction to continental collision, a process that helps explain how oceans disappear and mountain be
science.content: Researchers have identified two deep tears in the Arabian Plate beneath southeastern Iran, where the Zagros collision zone meets the Makran subduction zone. The structures offer evidence of the transition from oceanic subduction to continental collision, a process that helps explain how oceans disappear and mountain belts form. The team used seismic data recorded at 69 stations between March 2017 and September 2018 to map the plate at depth. The oceanic section beneath Makran extends to a depth of at least 450 kilometers, while continental lithosphere beneath Zagros reaches about 300 kilometers. Models suggest the tears may eventually join on a timescale of millions of years.
science.image_alt: Seismic study finds two deep tears in Arabian Plate beneath Iran

science.title: Rubin Observatory finds distant world that may qualify as a dwarf planet
science.summary: Astronomers using Chile’s Vera C. Rubin Observatory identified 2026 ED138, a distant object beyond Neptune that may be one of the largest known Kuiper Belt bodies. Its estimated diameter ranges from 600 to 1,500 kilometers, but researchers have not confirmed its size or whether it is round enough to qualify as a dwarf
science.content: Astronomers using Chile’s Vera C. Rubin Observatory identified 2026 ED138, a distant object beyond Neptune that may be one of the largest known Kuiper Belt bodies. Its estimated diameter ranges from 600 to 1,500 kilometers, but researchers have not confirmed its size or whether it is round enough to qualify as a dwarf planet. Astrophysicist Matthew Holman identified the object on Oct. 13 while reviewing telescope data. Researchers plan follow-up observations, particularly in infrared, to better determine its properties. Rubin Observatory is set to survey the southern sky repeatedly over the next decade, which could help reveal other faint, slowly moving objects.
science.image_alt: Rubin Observatory finds distant world that may qualify as a dwarf planet

science.title: Mantle uplift and ancient ice may explain Earth’s missing rock record
science.summary: A new study in Nature proposes that slow movements deep inside Earth lifted ancient continents, exposing them to erosion by massive ice sheets and creating the Great Unconformity—a gap in the rock record spanning hundreds of millions of years. The researchers used computer models of mantle movement to track continents
science.content: A new study in Nature proposes that slow movements deep inside Earth lifted ancient continents, exposing them to erosion by massive ice sheets and creating the Great Unconformity—a gap in the rock record spanning hundreds of millions of years. The researchers used computer models of mantle movement to track continents over the past billion years. The models indicate that the ancient landmasses Laurentia, Baltica and North China rose between about 1 billion and 540 million years ago, then sank. Glaciers during the Snowball Earth period could have scraped away exposed rock and sediment. The authors say their model helps explain why the gap is prominent in those regions, while other proposed causes remain under discussion.
science.image_alt: Mantle uplift and ancient ice may explain Earth’s missing rock record

science.title: Mars orbiter finds gas hinting at volcanic activity near Alba Mons
science.summary: The European Space Agency’s ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter detected hydrogen chloride above fissures near Alba Mons, Mars’ largest volcano by surface area, in observations that researchers say may indicate active magma underground. The unusual readings appeared in the northern hemisphere’s early summer, when the planet’s us
science.content: The European Space Agency’s ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter detected hydrogen chloride above fissures near Alba Mons, Mars’ largest volcano by surface area, in observations that researchers say may indicate active magma underground. The unusual readings appeared in the northern hemisphere’s early summer, when the planet’s usual atmospheric pattern would predict little hydrogen chloride. The researchers’ preferred explanation is that the gas escaped from a local igneous source through cracks as seasonal ice melted. The finding does not establish that Mars is erupting now: researchers also considered mud volcanoes and the breakdown of chlorine-bearing surface compounds as possible sources. The observations came from the orbiter’s 2021 data, and the study was published in *Science Advances*. Researchers say the fissures could be useful places to look for life because a subsurface magmatic system could support hydrothermal conditions with water, heat and nutrients; they reported no evidence of Martian life.
science.image_alt: Mars orbiter finds gas hinting at volcanic activity near Alba Mons

science.title: AST SpaceMobile taps Firefly engines for planned 2028 Blacklift rocket
science.summary: AST SpaceMobile has agreed to pay Firefly Aerospace more than $1.3 billion for engines, manufacturing rights and engineering support for Blacklift, a proposed rocket the satellite company aims to fly in late 2028. The reusable launcher is designed to carry up to five of AST’s BlueBird satellites per flight, giving the
science.content: AST SpaceMobile has agreed to pay Firefly Aerospace more than $1.3 billion for engines, manufacturing rights and engineering support for Blacklift, a proposed rocket the satellite company aims to fly in late 2028. The reusable launcher is designed to carry up to five of AST’s BlueBird satellites per flight, giving the company its own launch option as it builds its satellite network. The deal includes 36 engines for the first three rockets and an $800 million engine license, payable in $400 million in cash and $400 million in AST shares. Firefly retains the engine intellectual property. AST’s third-quarter earnings call is scheduled for Nov. 9, and the company plans to unveil Blacklift in New York on Nov. 12.
science.image_alt: AST SpaceMobile taps Firefly engines for planned 2028 Blacklift rocket

science.title: Delhi pollution reaches severe levels as court limits Diwali fireworks to green crackers
science.summary: Delhi’s air quality reached severe levels in many areas on Diwali morning, Nov. 8, with the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) above 400, Indian media reported. The previous morning, Swiss air-quality monitor IQAir ranked Delhi the world’s most polluted major city, with a U.S.-scale reading of 581. India’s Central Pollutio
science.content: Delhi’s air quality reached severe levels in many areas on Diwali morning, Nov. 8, with the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) above 400, Indian media reported. The previous morning, Swiss air-quality monitor IQAir ranked Delhi the world’s most polluted major city, with a U.S.-scale reading of 581. India’s Central Pollution Control Board recorded 363 on its separate scale, classified as “very poor”. India’s Supreme Court restricted fireworks to green crackers during specified hours, while authorities ordered schools around Delhi to move classes online and urged people to work from home. The court has also questioned the effectiveness of pollution controls and identified vehicle emissions as a major source. Light winds and winter conditions trap pollutants, while fires set to clear crop residue add smoke. More than 3,000 farm fires were reported in Punjab as the city’s air worsened.
science.image_alt: Delhi pollution reaches severe levels as court limits Diwali fireworks to green crackers

science.title: Climate shocks complicate Syrian refugees’ livelihoods in Turkey and recovery in Syria
science.summary: Climate-driven drought, heat and flooding are making it harder for Syrian refugees in Turkey to earn a living and for people returning to Syria to rebuild after war, according to reports on a new assessment by the United Nations refugee agency, UNHCR. Farm work that many refugees rely on has become less predictable. On
science.content: Climate-driven drought, heat and flooding are making it harder for Syrian refugees in Turkey to earn a living and for people returning to Syria to rebuild after war, according to reports on a new assessment by the United Nations refugee agency, UNHCR. Farm work that many refugees rely on has become less predictable. One Syrian beekeeper in Turkey said drought halved his honey production over five years, while later storms destroyed flowers his bees depend on. Nearly 90 million displaced people live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, UNHCR says. Nearly four million people have recently returned to Syria, where climate shocks threaten recovery. UNHCR warns that climate financing is not reaching many vulnerable communities. The COP31 climate conference is due to open in Antalya next week.
science.image_alt: Climate shocks complicate Syrian refugees’ livelihoods in Turkey and recovery in Syria

science.title: Pakistani astronaut set to become first foreign visitor to China’s station
science.summary: A Pakistani astronaut will fly as a payload specialist on China’s Shenzhou-24 mission, becoming the first foreign national to visit the Tiangong space station, China’s Manned Space Agency said on Nov. 7. The agency has not announced the astronaut’s identity or an official launch date. The mission is expected by year’s
science.content: A Pakistani astronaut will fly as a payload specialist on China’s Shenzhou-24 mission, becoming the first foreign national to visit the Tiangong space station, China’s Manned Space Agency said on Nov. 7. The agency has not announced the astronaut’s identity or an official launch date. The mission is expected by year’s end, while Pakistan’s Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said in October it was scheduled for Nov. 25. The visitor is due to stay briefly in orbit and return to Earth aboard Shenzhou-23, which docked with Tiangong in May. Pakistani candidates Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud trained in China; one will be selected for the flight and the other will serve as backup. The mission follows a 2025 Pakistan-China agreement to train Pakistani astronauts for space-station flights.
science.image_alt: Pakistani astronaut set to become first foreign visitor to China’s station

sports.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 to draw level with Barcelona
sports.summary: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday to provisionally draw level with La Liga leaders Barcelona on 30 points, extending their winning run under head coach José Mourinho to eight matches in all competitions. Barcelona can move clear again when it visits third-placed Atlético Madrid on Sunday. Federico Valverde open
sports.content: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday to provisionally draw level with La Liga leaders Barcelona on 30 points, extending their winning run under head coach José Mourinho to eight matches in all competitions. Barcelona can move clear again when it visits third-placed Atlético Madrid on Sunday. Federico Valverde opened the scoring in the 28th minute after Kylian Mbappé’s free kick rebounded off the wall, and Arda Güler made it 2-0 eight minutes later from a Jude Bellingham cross. Mbappé, who has scored in seven consecutive Real appearances, added the third in the 75th minute for his 13th league goal of the season. Valencia captain José Gayà was sent off four minutes later for fouling Mbappé as he broke through on goal. Real were without Vinícius Júnior, who was serving the last match of a four-game suspension, and have won all eight matches since losing to Atlético on September 20. The win came on a day of tributes to Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel, who died after a collision in a second-division match. Players paused in the ninth minute to mark his shirt number.
sports.image_alt: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 to draw level with Barcelona

sports.title: Rams activate Myles Garrett, setting up first pairing with Aaron Donald
sports.summary: The Los Angeles Rams activated defensive end Myles Garrett from injured reserve on Saturday, clearing the way for him to return against the Washington Commanders on Sunday and play alongside defensive tackle Aaron Donald for the first time. sports.content: The Los Angeles Rams activated defensive end Myles Garrett from injured reserve on Saturday, clearing the way for him to return against the Washington Commanders on Sunday and play alongside defensive tackle Aaron Donald for the first time. Garrett missed seven games after undergoing knee surgery following the season opener; Donald sat out that opener while rebuilding his fitness after returning from retirement. The Rams are 4-4 and tied for 26th in the NFL with 12 sacks, despite ranking third in quarterback pressure percentage. Garrett set the league’s single-season sack record with 23 last season, while Donald has yet to record a sack this year. Coach Sean McVay said Garrett is expected to play, barring a setback; his snap limit had not been determined.

sports.content: UFC chief executive Dana White confirmed at a boxing news conference in London on Saturday that he would meet President Donald Trump in Washington on Monday, Nov. 9, after Trump offered him the White House press secretary job. White did not say whether he would accept, joking that he already had many jobs. White leads the UFC and Power Slap and recently launched Zuffa Boxing. At the London news conference, he described plans to expand Zuffa Boxing and stage more international events. Trump’s post named six UFC fighters as potential assistants, including athletes from Russia, Brazil and the United States.

sports.content: Arsenal captain Martin Ødegaard scored in the 72nd minute to secure a 1-0 win over Hull City at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, November 7, moving the Premier League champions to 27 points after 10 matches. Their lead grew to six points when Manchester City lost 3-1 at Nottingham Forest later that day. Hull frustrated Arsenal with a disciplined defence, and goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis made several saves before Ødegaard scored from the rebound of Noni Madueke’s shot. The match also featured a disputed first-half decision after a video assistant referee (VAR) review: referee Farai Hallam acknowledged a shirt-pull on Kai Havertz but awarded Hull a free-kick after ruling Havertz offside. Arsenal have won nine of their first 10 league games, matching their best start in the competition, previously achieved in 2022-23. They head into the international break on top; Brighton could cut the gap to five points by beating Brentford on Sunday, November 8.

sports.content: No. 4 Notre Dame beat top-ranked Miami 31-24 in South Bend on Saturday, handing the Hurricanes their first loss. Quarterback CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns, while safety Luke Talich intercepted Miami quarterback Darian Mensah and broke up a fourth-down end-zone pass with 3:36 left to preserve the lead. Notre Dame built a 24-3 lead early in the third quarter before Miami twice rallied to within a touchdown. The Hurricanes played without leading receiver Malachi Toney, who was sidelined by an ankle injury. Mensah threw three touchdowns, but Miami could not complete the comeback. Notre Dame entered the weekend ranked No. 11 in the College Football Playoff standings. Miami beat Notre Dame 27-24 last season, a result that helped keep the Irish out of the playoff. Notre Dame has Boston College, SMU and Syracuse left in the regular season. The selection committee’s next rankings are due Tuesday, and Miami hosts Duke next Saturday.

sports.content: World No. 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew from the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Saturday, Nov. 7, because of a viral illness, ending her bid to defend the title before the season-ending tournament began. The 27-year-old Kazakh said she was not physically ready to play and would rest at home before preparing for 2027. Ukraine’s Marta Kostyuk, the first alternate, takes Rybakina’s place in Group 1 and is scheduled to open against Linda Noskova on Sunday; Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula are also in the group. Rybakina finishes her season with a 54-14 record and four titles, including the Australian Open and US Open, and has already secured the year-end No. 1 ranking. Rybakina also withdrew from the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo in October with a neck injury, but the WTA identified a viral illness as the reason for her latest withdrawal. Her exit leaves the field without the reigning champion; she won the 2025 Finals without losing a match.

sports.content: Jon Rahm will take a one-shot lead over Tyrrell Hatton and Francesco Laporta into Sunday’s final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links. Rahm stands at 18 under par, with Rory McIlroy two shots back in fourth. Rahm shot a bogey-free 66 on Saturday; Hatton and Laporta each carded 67, while McIlroy’s 67 included a double bogey on the 10th and a bogey on the 17th. McIlroy is also pursuing a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai season title, but his two-shot deficit matches the penalty he received in Thursday’s opening round for improving his lie. He said he would need a round in the mid-to-low 60s to contend. The Abu Dhabi event is the first of two DP World Tour playoff tournaments: the top 50 players in this week’s 70-player field advance to next week’s $10 million finale in Dubai.

sports.content: Carlos Alcaraz reached his first Paris Masters final on Saturday with a 6-4, 6-4 win over Casper Ruud, while Ben Shelton rallied past Frenchman Luca Van Assche 5-7, 6-3, 6-4. The world No. 3 and No. 4 meet for the title on Sunday, Nov. 8. The two meet again two months after Shelton beat Alcaraz in a five-set US Open quarter-final. Alcaraz leads their head-to-head record 3-1 but lost their most recent meeting. He reached the Paris final after saving two match points against Taylor Fritz on Friday. Alcaraz enters on an eight-match winning streak after winning the Vienna title last week. Both players are contesting their sixth tour-level final of the season. Alcaraz is seeking his first Paris title, having never previously advanced beyond the quarter-finals; Shelton is seeking his third Masters-level title.
